Required by GET /v1/vaults/{vault}/tokens/{token}, by a token template reference in a /v1/proxy body, and by creating a `detokenize` route action. Distinct from vaults:read, which lists vaults and token metadata and never returns a value.
scopes.transit:decrypt: Open a portable `kc:` ciphertext with a tenant transit key. Required by creating a `decrypt` route action, which stores a standing instruction to open every matching field on every later request through that route. It is the same capability name the policy engine uses for POST /v1/decrypt. No routes scope satisfies it — managing a route is not permission to open the data flowing through it.
scopes.proxy:invoke: Call the one-shot ephemeral proxy (any method on /v1/proxy). Required for EVERY verb — the proxy is one capability behind one handler, and a bodyless GET spends an escrowed credential exactly as a POST does. Neither proxy:read nor proxy:write satisfies it.

PhantomToken.description:
The AI **data plane** credential — a `kp_`-prefixed capability token, not a
Management API credential. It is minted per agent (or per MCP resource) at
`POST /v1/ai-gateway/agents/{agentId}/tokens`, or exchanged from a CI workload's
OIDC token at `POST /v1/oauth/token`, and it is the ONLY credential `/v1/ai/*`
accepts: an OAuth `kc_` access token or a `tk_` API key is refused there, and a
`kp_` token is refused on `api.knoxcall.com`.

Three header spellings are accepted, so an existing provider SDK can be pointed at
the agent URL without rewriting its auth:

    Authorization: Bearer kp_live_a_...
    x-api-key: kp_live_a_...
    x-knox-ai-key: kp_live_a_...

`kp_live_` is refused on the sandbox host and `kp_test_` on the Live host — the env
segment is enforced, not cosmetic. DPoP-bound tokens additionally require a valid
`DPoP` proof header on every request, signed over the canonical public URL rather
than a rewritten `Host`.

A rejected credential answers `401`/`403` in the data-plane error envelope with the
cause in `code` and in the `X-Auth-Failure` response header.

BearerAuth.description:
Legacy long-lived API key authentication via the Authorization header.
Pass your API key as: `Authorization: Bearer tk_xxx_yyy`.

Standard keys (`tk_` prefix) are accepted on `api.knoxcall.com`.
Test keys (type=test) are accepted on `sandbox.knoxcall.com`.
Enterprise Access Keys (`AKE` prefix) are accepted on both.

Fully supported, but prefer the `OAuth2` scheme (or the SDKs, which handle
OAuth for you) for new integrations.

ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyAuth.description:
Legacy API key authentication via the `x-api-key` header.
This is an alternative to Bearer token authentication for clients that cannot
set the `Authorization` header. Prefer the `OAuth2` scheme for new integrations.

CapabilityTokenAuth.description:
Single-use client capability token (`kct_` prefix), passed as
`Authorization: Bearer kct_...`. Minted server-side via
`POST /client-tokens` and bound either to one exact payload + action
(`decrypt`, `detokenize`) or to one vault + a closed set of page
origins (`tokenize`). This is NOT an API key — it authenticates only
the `POST /client/decrypt`, `POST /client/detokenize` and
`POST /client/tokenize` consume endpoints and is invalidated after its
first use.

PageParam.name: page
PageParam.description: Page number for pagination. Clamped server-side so the derived offset never exceeds 100,000 rows -- the effective maximum is `floor(100000 / per_page) + 1`, i.e. 1,001 at `per_page=100`. A larger value returns that last page, and `meta.page` reports it.

ApiVersionParam.name: KnoxCall-Version
ApiVersionParam.description: Pin to a dated API version (`YYYY-MM-DD`); omitted → newest. Unknown version → `400 invalid_api_version`. Applies to every operation; the resolved version is echoed in the `KnoxCall-Version` response header.

KnoxProxyUrlHeader.name: X-Knox-Proxy-URL
KnoxProxyUrlHeader.description: The HTTPS upstream URL to forward the request to. Must use a DNS hostname (no IP literals).

IdempotencyKeyParam.name: X-Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyParam.description:
Optional idempotency key so a retried mutating request is executed at most once.
The standard `Idempotency-Key` spelling is also accepted. Replaying a completed
request with the same key returns the original stored response with an
`X-Idempotent-Replay: true` header. A key still in progress returns
`409 request_in_progress`; the same key with a different body returns
`422 idempotency_key_reuse`; a malformed key returns `400 invalid_idempotency_key`.

SortParam.name: sort
SortParam.description:
Field to sort the result set by. The set of accepted fields varies per endpoint;
pair with `order` (`asc`/`desc`) to control direction.

EnabledParam.name: enabled
EnabledParam.description: Filter the result set to only enabled (`true`) or only disabled (`false`) resources.

RequestMeta.description: Metadata included with every API response.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request, useful for support and debugging.

total.description: Total number of records matching the query.

total_pages.description: Total number of pages, capped at the deepest page the 100,000-row offset ceiling allows -- `min(ceil(total / per_page), floor(100000 / per_page) + 1)`. When it is below `ceil(total / per_page)` the result set is larger than pagination can reach; narrow it with a filter.

request_id.description: Unique identifier for this API request.

type.description: Machine-readable error type. The set is OPEN — endpoints define specific types beyond the common ones below, so clients should branch on the types they know and fall back to the HTTP status class for anything unrecognized. Common values: authentication_required, invalid_api_key, wrong_key_type, subscription_inactive, rate_limit_exceeded, validation_error, forbidden, not_found, method_not_allowed (405, carries Allow), conflict, in_use, plan_limit, plan_feature, internal_error, dependency_unavailable (503, carries Retry-After), invalid_request, invalid_definition, not_cancellable, invalid_idempotency_key, idempotency_key_reuse, request_in_progress, system_client_protected, use_oauth, use_dpop_nonce (401 on /v1 and the data plane, 400 on POST /oauth/token; see "DPoP sender-constrained tokens").

EgressObservation.description: One (host, first path segment, method, credential header NAME) key the SDK's interceptor saw a credential leave for without interception, with how often and when. Never a credential value, a full path, a query string or a body — the server drops an entry carrying any of those.

host.description: Bare DNS hostname. The server lower-cases it, strips a trailing dot, converts an IDN to punycode and drops a port — the same normalisation the intercept manifest applies to a Route's target. A scheme, path, query or userinfo is refused (`invalid_host`); an IP literal (`ip_literal`) and any KnoxCall host (`own_host`) are dropped.

first_segment.description: `/` or `/<one segment>` — no deeper path, no query string.

header_name.description: Lower-case NAME of the header the credential travelled in, from the shared allowlist (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, `apikey`, `x-apikey`, `x-auth-token`, `x-access-token`, `x-token`, `token`, `x-secret`, `x-secret-key`, `x-client-secret`, `ocp-apim-subscription-key`, `x-goog-api-key`, `x-amz-security-token`, `x-shopify-access-token`, `klaviyo-api-key`, `x-hubspot-api-key`) or any name ending in `-api-key`, `-token`, `-secret` or `-auth`. Anything else is dropped (`invalid_header_name`). The value is never sent.

count.description: Calls observed for this key in the reported interval.

first_seen.description: ISO-8601 with an offset. Older than 7 days is dropped (`stale`).

last_seen.description: ISO-8601 with an offset, not before `first_seen`, not more than 5 minutes ahead of the server clock (`future`). Its UTC calendar day is the row the entry merges into.

sdk.description: The reporting SDK and its version, `<name>/<version>`.

observations.description: At most 200 per request; more is a `413`.

EgressObservationReceipt.description: What happened to the batch. `accepted + dropped` equals the number of observations sent.

accepted.description: Entries merged into the space's observations.

dropped.description: Entries refused, each counted under exactly one reason.

reasons.description: Dropped entries per reason. Keys are from the closed set `malformed`, `invalid_host`, `ip_literal`, `own_host`, `invalid_first_segment`, `invalid_method`, `invalid_header_name`, `invalid_count`, `invalid_timestamp`, `stale`, `future`, `daily_cap`; a reason with no drops is omitted.

redacted.description: Accepted entries that were altered before storage, per reason. The one reason today is `first_segment_looks_like_credential`: a first path segment that looks like it carries a secret (a Telegram `bot<id>:<token>`, a known key prefix, a long or high-entropy token) is stored as `/`, so a credential value never reaches a row. A reason with no redactions is omitted.

InterceptManifest.description: GET /wrap/intercept-manifest. Which upstream hosts an intercept-enabled Route covers for one environment of this space.

version.description: Content hash of `routes`; doubles as the ETag.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the SDK should hold this manifest before polling again.

routes.description: Sorted by host, then longest `base_path` first, then slug — the order a longest-prefix match reads.

host.description: Lower-case DNS hostname, no port, trailing dot stripped.

base_path.description: Path prefix the route serves under (`/` when its target has none). The SDK forwards the request path with this prefix removed; a request not under any listed prefix for the host is not a route match.

requires_clients.description: The environment requires a registered client (IP, mTLS or signed assertion). A bearer-only SDK call will be refused; the SDK warns at install and never falls back.

allowed_methods.description: Upper-cased verbs when method restrictions are on for this environment; null otherwise.

ambiguous.description: Present and true when another entry shares this (host, base_path); the SDK takes the lexically lowest slug and warns.

RouteSummary.description: Summary representation of a route returned in list responses.

name.description: Unique human-readable route name, used as the URL path segment.

slug.description: Write-once machine handle for code references (like a Stripe lookup_key). Null when unset.

target_base_url.description: The upstream URL that requests are forwarded to.

enabled.description: Whether the route is active and accepting requests.

require_signature.description: Whether request signature verification is required.

rate_limit_enabled.description: Whether per-route rate limiting is active.

rate_limit_requests.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per rate limit window.

rate_limit_window_sec.description: Rate limit window duration in seconds.

allowed_methods.description: List of allowed HTTP methods. Null means all methods are allowed.

intercept_enabled.description: Whether this route participates in transparent interception — the agent's intercept mode AND the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()` route calls to its target host through it. Per environment; this view is the base environment's value. See GET /wrap/intercept-manifest.

requires_clients.description: Whether requests must come from an authorized client.

collection_id.description: Collection this route belongs to, if any.

Route.description:
Full route row as returned after create or update operations. Runtime
injection/rate-limit configuration lives in the per-environment
configs (see `GET /routes/{id}/environments`), not on this row.

slug.description: Write-once machine handle for code references. Null when unset.

sandbox.description: Whether this route lives in Test (sandbox) mode.

target_base_url.description:
Derived read-only view of the base environment's target URL. Set
it per environment via the environment-config endpoints; the
value accepted on create seeds the base environment's config.

intercept_enabled.description: Whether this route participates in transparent interception — the agent's intercept mode AND the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()` route calls to its target host through it. Per environment; this view is the base environment's value. See GET /wrap/intercept-manifest.

requires_clients.description:
Derived read-only view of the base environment's setting. Client
authorization is per-environment; set it via PATCH (fans out to
every environment) or the environment-config endpoints.

mtls_certificate_id.description:
Derived read-only view of the base environment's mTLS binding
(certificate-type secret used for upstream mTLS). Per-environment
since migration 20260723.

egress_server_id.description: Derived read-only view of the base environment's egress server.

RouteDetail.description:
Route detail as returned by `GET /routes/{id}`. The
`payload_structure`, `injection_rules`, `ip_allowlist`, and
`data_plane_node_id` fields are present only when the route has a
base-environment configuration row. `injection_rules` is deprecated and
is applied to no request — see the field's own description.

slug.description: Write-once machine handle for code references. Null when unset.

target_base_url.description: Derived read-only view of the base environment's target URL.

intercept_enabled.description: Whether this route participates in transparent interception — the agent's intercept mode AND the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()` route calls to its target host through it. Per environment; this view is the base environment's value. See GET /wrap/intercept-manifest.

configured_environments.description: Names of environments that have overrides configured.

payload_structure.description:
The base environment's saved sample request body, as its
**structure only** — the same keys and nesting, with every value
replaced by a type placeholder: `"<string>"`, `"<number>"` or
`"<boolean>"` (`null` stays `null`; arrays keep each element,
projected the same way). Present only when a base-environment
config exists.

The sample's values are never returned by the API, whatever the
key's scopes and whatever the query string: a saved sample is
usually a captured request, so its values are a recorded,
step-up-gated reveal for an Admin or the Owner in the dashboard.

injection_rules.description:
**Deprecated and never applied.** Present only when a base-environment
config exists, and echoed here only so a legacy value written through
the dashboard remains visible. It is applied to no request, and
`POST /routes` and `PATCH /routes/{id}` now reject a non-empty value.
Body secret injection works by placing `{{secret_id:<uuid>}}` or
`{{secret:<name>}}` placeholders in the request body your client
sends, for a secret the route's own templates already send; any
other secret is refused with 403 `client_placeholder_not_bound`
(accounts created before that rule was deployed are report-only
until switched over: the placeholder resolves and each use is
audited). Do not send this field back in an update.

ip_allowlist.description: Present only when a base-environment config exists.

data_plane_node_id.description: Present only when a base-environment config exists.

name.description: Unique name for the route. This becomes the URL path segment used to proxy requests.

slug.description:
Write-once machine handle for code references. Omit to derive a
`{collection}-{name}` default; pass null for no slug. Lowercase
letters, numbers, and hyphens; cannot look like a UUID; immutable
once set.

target_base_url.description: The upstream URL that requests will be forwarded to. Resolved and SSRF-checked at write time: a private, loopback or link-local address, or any KnoxCall-owned host (`*.knoxcall.com`), is refused with `400 ssrf_blocked` — routes never target the platform that serves them.

base_environment.description: Default environment for the route. Must be an existing environment name.

inject_headers_json.description: Headers to inject. Use `{{SECRET_NAME}}` to reference secrets.

inject_body_json.description: Body fields to inject. Use `{{SECRET_NAME}}` to reference secrets.

injection_rules.description:
**Removed — a non-empty value is rejected with 400.** It was stored
and applied to nothing. Use `{{secret_id:<uuid>}}` /
`{{secret:<name>}}` placeholders in the request body your client
sends, for a secret the route's own templates already send (any
other is refused with 403 `client_placeholder_not_bound`, except
on accounts created before that rule was deployed, which are
report-only until switched over). An empty array is still
accepted as a no-op.

ip_allowlist.description: IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to call this route.

collection_id.description: Assign this route to a collection.

UpdateRouteRequest.description: All fields are optional. Only provided fields will be updated.

slug.description:
Write-once: settable only while the route has no slug; immutable
forever after (requests to change an existing slug return 400).

egress_server_id.description: Route traffic through this egress server. Must be owned by or allocated to your account.

data_plane_node_id.description: Pin the route to a data-plane node you own (or a shared managed node).

intercept_enabled.description: Opt this route into transparent interception (agent intercept mode and the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()`). Per environment. Must be a boolean; anything else answers `400`.

injection_rules.description:
**Removed — a non-empty value is rejected with 400.** It was stored
and applied to nothing. Use `{{secret_id:<uuid>}}` /
`{{secret:<name>}}` placeholders in the request body your client
sends, for a secret the route's own templates already send (any
other is refused with 403 `client_placeholder_not_bound`, except
on accounts created before that rule was deployed, which are
report-only until switched over). An empty array is still
accepted as a no-op.

method_configs.description:
Per-HTTP-method overrides for the route's base environment. A saved
sample is read back as its structure only (see
`RouteEnvironmentConfig.method_configs`), so an entry whose
`payload_structure` equals that structure keeps the stored sample
rather than replacing it with its placeholders; any other
`payload_structure` is saved as sent.

RouteEnvironmentConfig.description: Environment-specific configuration override for a route.

environment_name.description: The environment this override applies to.

target_base_url.description: Override upstream URL for this environment.

inject_headers_json.description: Override injected headers for this environment.

inject_body_json.description: Override injected body fields for this environment.

intercept_enabled.description: Whether this route participates in transparent interception — the agent's intercept mode AND the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()` route calls to its target host through it. Per environment; this view is the base environment's value. See GET /wrap/intercept-manifest.

requires_clients.description: Whether requests in this environment must come from an authorized client.

mtls_certificate_id.description: Certificate-type secret used for upstream mTLS in this environment.

egress_server_id.description: Egress server (static IP) for this environment. Null means direct.

enabled.description:
Per-environment serving switch. False pauses this environment
only; the route-level `enabled` flag disables every environment.

payload_structure.description:
This environment's saved sample request body, as its **structure
only**: the same keys and nesting, each value replaced by a type
placeholder (`"<string>"`, `"<number>"`, `"<boolean>"`; `null`
stays `null`). The values are never returned by the API.

method_configs.description:
Per-HTTP-method overrides for this environment. A `payload_structure`
inside an entry is returned as its structure only, exactly like the
environment's own `payload_structure`; every other field of the
entry is returned as stored.

RouteEnvironmentConfigInput.description:
Fields for creating or updating an environment override. All fields are optional;
only provided fields are set. Existing fields not included in the request are preserved.

intercept_enabled.description: Opt this route into transparent interception (agent intercept mode and the SDKs' `wrap.intercept()`). Per environment. Must be a boolean; anything else answers `400`.

RequestLog.description:
A record of a proxied API request.

On `GET /logs` the fields `id`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `route_id`,
`matched_client_id`, `identification_method`, `method`, `status_code`,
`src_ip`, `environment`, `sandbox` and `ts` are exactly what the Merkle
anchor commits to, in that order - see `GET /logs/{request_id}/proof`.
Every other field is operational detail and is NOT part of the leaf.

id.description: Row id as a decimal string. This is `api_requests.id`, a bigint - NOT a uuid, which earlier revisions of this schema incorrectly declared. It is a string rather than a JSON number because a JSON number is a double and cannot hold a bigint exactly past 2^53.

request_id.description: Correlation ID for the proxied request.

src_ip.description: Source IP address of the caller, host form without a prefix length. Identity tier on `GET /logs`: requires `log:read_identity`, and is ABSENT (not null) when denied.

status_code.description: HTTP status code returned by the upstream.

upstream_host.description: Upstream host the request was forwarded to.

error.description: Error message if the request failed.

environment.description: Environment the request was resolved against.

signature_valid.description: Whether the request signature was valid (if required).

source_ip_country.description: Country of the source IP (GeoIP lookup).

source_ip_city.description: City of the source IP (GeoIP lookup).

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant. Returned by `GET /logs`; omitted by `GET /routes/{id}/logs`.

matched_client_id.description: Which client the request was attributed to. Kept when that client is later deleted, so it may name a client that no longer exists: it is a committed field of the row's Merkle leaf and is never rewritten. Identity tier on `GET /logs`: requires `log:read_identity`, and is ABSENT (not null) when denied.

identification_method.description: How that attribution was made (e.g. `ip`, `mtls_thumbprint`). Identity tier on `GET /logs`.

sandbox.description: Live/Test partition. `null` on rows written before the partition existed, which are treated as Live. Null, false and true are three distinct facts and the Merkle anchor keeps them apart.

cursor.description: Opaque resume token, returned by `GET /logs` only. Pass the last row's value as `cursor` on the next call.

client_origin.description: How the call arrived at the Route. `sdk_intercept`: a KnoxCall SDK's route-aware interceptor rerouted a third-party SDK's request onto the Route (the SDK sent `x-knoxcall-origin: sdk-intercept`). `direct`: a plain `call()` / bound-route request, and every row written before the marker existed. Informational only - it never influences authentication, routing, rate limits or the response block.

Opportunity.description: A promotion suggestion (agent_monitor or gateway_traffic source).

evidence_json.description: Detection evidence (call_count, active_days, methods, window). Host-only — never a path/body/credential.

Secret.description:
Secret metadata. Secret values are never returned by the API. Reference
secrets in route injection configs using `{{SECRET_NAME}}` syntax.

name.description: The secret name (spaces normalized to underscores).

shortcode_name.description: Short name used in template references.

environment_count.description: Number of environments this secret has values configured in.

collection_id.description: Collection this secret belongs to, if any.

expires_at.description: When the secret expires. Null for no expiry. On write, must be within 20 years of now — far-future sentinels like 9999-12-31 are rejected with 400.

strict_expiry_enforcement.description: When true, the proxy refuses to inject the secret after it expires.

SecretEnvironmentVersion.description:
Per-environment metadata for a secret. Returned by
`GET /secrets/{id}`; never contains the value.

value_version.description:
Counter of genuine value writes for this environment, starting at 1
when the environment's first value is stored. Incremented ONLY by
writes that change the stored value — rotations through
`PUT /secrets/{id}/value`, admin value and certificate updates, and
platform-managed custodial key rotation.

Deliberately NOT incremented by writes that leave the value
unchanged: OAuth2 token refreshes, expiry-override edits,
certificate metadata re-parsing, environment renames, or a
re-encryption of the same plaintext under a new tenant key (BYOK
rewrap). `updated_at` moves for all of those, which is why it
cannot be used as a rotation signal.

updated_at.description:
When this environment's row last changed for ANY reason — including
non-value writes. Use `value_version` to detect value changes.

expires_at_override.description:
Per-environment expiry override. Null means the environment
inherits the secret-level `expires_at`.

SecretDetail.description:
A secret plus its per-environment metadata. Returned by
`GET /secrets/{id}`; the list endpoint returns the base `Secret` shape.

environments.description:
One entry per environment that has a value, ordered by
environment name.

OAuth2Token.description: An auto-refreshing OAuth2 access token retrieved from an OAuth2-type secret.

expires_at.description: When the access token expires. Null if unknown.

connection_status.description: Current status of the OAuth2 connection.

CreateSecretRequest.description:
Creates a secret. Set `secret_type` to choose the variant:
- `string` (default) — requires `name` and `value`
- `oauth2` — requires OAuth2 fields (see `CreateOAuth2SecretRequest`)
- `certificate` — requires certificate fields (see `CreateCertificateSecretRequest`)

secret_type.description: Omit or set to `string` for a static value secret.

name.description: Secret name. Spaces are replaced with underscores.

value.description: The secret value to encrypt and store.

collection_id.description: Assign this secret to a collection.

strict_expiry_enforcement.description: When true, the proxy refuses to inject the secret after it expires.

secret_type.description: Must be `oauth2` when using this schema via `POST /secrets`.

name.description: Secret name. Spaces are replaced with underscores.

provider.description:
OAuth2 provider. Use `custom` for any provider not listed — you must then supply
`auth_url` and `token_url`.

client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID (from your provider's developer console).

client_secret.description:
OAuth2 client secret. Required unless using `mtls_certificate_id` for mTLS auth
or `grant_type: implicit`.

grant_type.description:
OAuth2 grant type:
- `authorization_code` (default) — redirects user to `redirect_uri` for consent
- `client_credentials` — server-to-server; tokens fetched immediately
- `password` — ROPC flow; requires `username` and `password`
- `implicit` — legacy browser flow (not recommended)

scopes.description: OAuth2 scopes to request. Defaults to the provider's recommended scopes.

auth_url.description:
Authorization endpoint URL. Accepted only when `provider` is `custom` — for every
other provider the platform's known default is used and this field is ignored.
Must be an absolute `https://` URL with no embedded credentials and no `#`
fragment; anything else is rejected with `validation_error`. A query string is
allowed (Azure AD B2C's `?p=<policy>`) and is preserved.

token_url.description:
Token endpoint URL. Accepted only when `provider` is `custom` — for every other
provider the platform's known default is used and this field is ignored. Must be
an absolute `https://` URL with no embedded credentials and no `#` fragment;
`http://` is rejected because this endpoint receives the client secret.

mtls_certificate_id.description:
ID of a `certificate`-type secret to use for mTLS authentication to the token
endpoint instead of `client_secret`.

collection_id.description: Assign this secret to a collection.

OAuth2SecretCreated.description: Response after creating an OAuth2 secret.

name.description: Normalized secret name.

redirect_uri.description:
The OAuth2 callback URL pre-configured for this secret. For `authorization_code`
flows, redirect your user here to initiate authorization. Register this URI in
your provider's OAuth2 app settings.

connection_status.description: Initial status is always `not_connected` until the OAuth2 flow completes.

secret_type.description: Must be `certificate` when using this schema via `POST /secrets`.

name.description: Secret name. Spaces are replaced with underscores.

certificate_content.description:
The certificate in PEM, PKCS#7, CRT/CER format, or as a base64-encoded DER/PFX/P12
blob. For PEM, include the full `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` block.

private_key.description:
Optional PEM-encoded private key. If provided, it is combined with the certificate
content before encryption.

passphrase.description:
Optional passphrase to decrypt the private key. Encrypted and stored separately
from the certificate.

certificate_type.description:
Format of the certificate content:
- `pem` / `crt` / `cer` — PEM-encoded X.509 certificate (metadata auto-extracted)
- `pkcs7` / `p7b` / `p7c` — PKCS#7 certificate bundle (metadata auto-extracted)
- `pfx` / `p12` — Binary PKCS#12 bundle (pass as base64)
- `key` — Standalone private key

collection_id.description: Assign this secret to a collection.

CertificateSecretCreated.description: Response after creating a certificate secret.

name.description: Normalized secret name.

metadata.description:
Parsed certificate metadata (for PEM, CRT, CER, PKCS#7 formats). Null fields
indicate the value could not be extracted from the certificate.

issuer.example: CN=Let's Encrypt Authority X3, O=Let's Encrypt, C=US

has_private_key.description: Whether a private key was stored alongside the certificate.

has_passphrase.description: Whether a passphrase was stored for the private key. The platform never returns the passphrase itself; this boolean is the only confirmation that one was received and stored.

Client.description: An authorized client (user or server) with IP-based access control.

name.description: Human-readable name for the client.

type.description: Client type -- `user` for individual users, `server` for backend services.

ip_address.description: IP address, CIDR range, or IP range authorized for this client.

collection_id.description: Collection this client belongs to, if any.

ClientFull.description: Full client row as returned by create and update operations.

name.description: Human-readable name for the client.

type.description: Client type. Defaults to `server` if not specified.

ip_address.description:
IP address or CIDR range to authorize. Supports individual IPs (e.g. `203.0.113.42`),
CIDR notation (e.g. `203.0.113.0/24`), and IPv6 addresses.

UpdateClientRequest.description: All fields are optional. Only provided fields will be updated.

Environment.description: A deployment environment used to scope route configurations.

name.description: Machine-readable name (lowercase, hyphens, underscores only).

color.description: Hex color code for UI display. Exactly six hex digits with a leading '#'.

is_default.description: Whether this is the default environment.

name.description:
Machine-readable name. Must contain only lowercase letters, numbers,
hyphens, and underscores.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name. Defaults to the `name` value.

is_default.description: Set this environment as the default. Only one environment can be default.

ApiKey.description: An API key (masked -- full key is only returned at creation time).

id.description: Internal UUID of the key record.

key_prefix.description: First few characters of the key for identification.

key_type.description:
Type of the API key. `standard` keys work on the production API,
`test` keys work on the sandbox API, `access_key` keys work on both.

name.description: Human-readable name for the key.

active.description: Whether the key is active (false if revoked).

last_used_at.description: Timestamp of the last time this key was used.

expires_at.description:
When this key stops authenticating. `null` means it **never expires** — it stays
valid until someone revokes it by hand.

Expiry is enforced on every authentication path, so a key past this instant is
`401` everywhere, with no way to extend it: an expired key is replaced, not
renewed.

**A key created without an explicit expiry choice gets 90 days.** That default
is applied when the key is minted, so this field is the only place it is
visible — read it on every key, including ones you did not create.

ApiKeyCreated.description:
API key creation response. The `api_key` field contains the full key and is
**only returned once** at creation time. Store it securely.

Internal UUID of the key record — the value `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}` and
role assignments reference. Added 2026-08-09; previously the create response
carried no UUID at all, so a caller had to list keys back to find it.

role_ids.description:
The role UUIDs actually attached, in the same transaction as the key. Empty
when none were requested — which means the key is default-denied on every
policy-gated endpoint.

api_key.description:
The full API key. **This is the only time it will be shown.** Store it
in a secure location immediately.

key_prefix.description: First characters of the key for identification.

key_type.description: Key type determined by which API host the key was created on.

name.description: Name you assigned to the key.

expires_at.description:
When the new key stops authenticating, resolved from whichever of
`expires_in_days` / `expires_at` / `never_expires` you sent. `null` means it
never expires.

**Sending none of the three puts this 90 days out**, so read this field back
even when you did not ask for an expiry — it is the value that was actually
applied, not an echo of your request.

message.description: Reminder to store the key securely.
message.example: Store this API key securely. It will not be shown again.

name.description: Human-readable name to identify this key.

rate_limit_requests.description: Maximum requests per rate limit window. Leave empty for no rate limit.

rate_limit_window_sec.description: Rate limit window in seconds. Required if `rate_limit_requests` is set.

expires_in_days.description:
Lifetime in days, counted from the moment the key is minted.

**At most one** of `expires_in_days`, `expires_at` and `never_expires` may be
present; two or more is `400 conflicting_expiry_fields`. A value outside
1-365 is `400 invalid_expiry`.

**Omitting all three is not a way to opt out of expiry** — the key gets the
default 90 days. To create a key that never expires you must say so, with
`never_expires: true`.

expires_at.description:
Exact expiry instant, ISO 8601. Must be in the future and no more than 365 days
from now, else `400 invalid_expiry`. Mutually exclusive with `expires_in_days`
and `never_expires` (`400 conflicting_expiry_fields`).

Use this when the key's life is pinned to a date you already know — a contract
end, an audit window — rather than to a duration.

never_expires.description:
Send `true` for a key with **no expiry**: the response and every later read
carry `expires_at: null`, and the key stays valid until it is revoked by hand.
A key that never stops working also never stops working for whoever finds it in
an old CI secret or a container image, so this is a deliberate choice and not a
default.

Mutually exclusive with `expires_in_days` and `expires_at`
(`400 conflicting_expiry_fields`). `false` is refused with
`400 invalid_expiry` rather than quietly meaning "use the default" — a body
that mentions expiry at all is making a statement about it, and answering that
statement with a silent 90-day clock is the guess this field exists to remove.

role_ids.description:
Permission roles to attach to the new key, assigned in the SAME transaction as
the key itself. Discover ids with `GET /v1/roles?subject_kind=api_key`.

Omit (or send `[]`) to create a key with no role — such a key is
**default-denied on every policy-gated endpoint**, which is rarely what you
want. For an infrastructure-as-code runner, attach the seeded
`Key — Infrastructure` role.

Every id must (a) belong to your tenant, else `404`; (b) declare the `api_key`
audience in `applies_to`, else `400`; (c) grant nothing the calling key
does not itself hold, else `403 privilege_escalation`; and (d) be one of the
SEEDED key roles (`Key — Invoke`, `Key — Read-only`, `Key — Editor`,
`Key — Infrastructure`), else `403 forbidden`. A key can never mint a key more
privileged than itself. Custom roles are being retired in favour of per-key
permissions: a custom role a key already holds keeps working, but no new key
can be given one.

Role.description:
A named bundle of permission policies. Read-only on `/v1`, and exposed so a machine
can discover the id to pass in `role_ids`. The seeded roles (`seeded: true`) are
platform-managed and cannot be renamed or recomposed; custom roles are being retired
in favour of fixed roles and per-key permissions, so no new custom role can be
created and only a seeded key role can be given to a new key.

The rules a role grants are deliberately NOT exposed — enumerating them would map
the tenant's authorization surface to every machine credential in it.

name.description: Display name. The seeded machine roles are `Key — Invoke`, `Key — Read-only`, `Key — Editor` and `Key — Infrastructure`.

description.example: For Terraform and other infrastructure-as-code runners.

is_default.description: Whether the admin UI prefills this role when creating a new key.

seeded.description: True for roles the platform creates and maintains (they cannot be deleted, renamed or recomposed). Only a seeded key role is accepted in `role_ids`; custom roles (`false`) are being retired.

one cannot be produced. Carries every field of `RequestLog` in addition
to those below.

verified.description: Whether the anchored range still recomputes to the root the anchor recorded. Absent when `anchored` is false.

reason.description: Present only when no proof is returned. See the endpoint description for what each value means.

observed_leaf_count.description: Rows the range holds now, when that differs from what the anchor counted.

recomputed_root.description: The root the range produces now. Present only on `root_mismatch`.

anchor.description: The anchor row this proof stands on.

sequence_number.description: Position in the hash-chained critical audit log, as a decimal string.

merkle_root.description: Hex-encoded root committed by the anchor.

verification.description: Everything needed to redo this computation without trusting KnoxCall.

When set, a request whose upstream endpoint KnoxCall cannot classify as serving that region is refused on the data plane with HTTP 403 `residency_violation` — including a fallback route, which is where an unpinned failover would otherwise leave the region. `null` (the default) applies no residency constraint. tags.description: FinOps attribution labels (cost_center/team/project/…) echoed onto this agent's usage rows.

provider.description: The upstream shape this agent fronts — one of the values `CreateAiGatewayAgentRequest.provider` enumerates (the catalog has grown to fourteen; `ai_gateway_agents_provider_check` is the authority). routing_policy.description: Returned on every agent read. `{}` — the default for every agent — means one attempt per route and fail-over to `fallback_route_ids` on 5xx only.

guardrail_webhook_mode.description: Which directions are inspected. `off` when the agent has no hook — the server returns the string, never a boolean.

guardrail_webhook_timeout_ms.description: How long the gateway waits for a verdict. Defaults to 2000.

guardrail_webhook_failure_action.description: What happens when the hook does not answer. Defaults to `fail_open`, the posture an agent already has with no hook at all.

The data-plane base URL for this agent — `https://{tenant}.knoxcall.com/v1/ai/{slug}`.
Point an AI SDK's `base_url` here and give it a capability token as the API key.

Present on EVERY agent projection: create, get, update and the list rows (AIGW-160
era it was create and get only, so a list row was shaped differently from the row
create returned). It is server-computed rather than stored, so it MOVES when `slug`
changes — which is why `PATCH` returns it too.

An EMPTY STRING when the tenant slug cannot be resolved. Treat empty as "not
available", never as a URL.

primary_route_id.description: The route the agent's upstream calls are proxied through. Pass this OR `provider` + `upstream_secret_id`, never both.

provider.description:
Name a provider and KnoxCall composes the upstream route for you, injecting the credential from `upstream_secret_id`. Requires `upstream_secret_id`, and forbids `primary_route_id`.

Ten of these speak the OpenAI Chat Completions API (openai, azure-openai, ollama, groq, together, mistral, deepseek, fireworks, xai, openai-compatible), so an OpenAI SDK works unchanged — point it at the agent URL plus the provider's OpenAI sub-path (`/v1`, or `/openai/v1` for azure-openai and groq).

`bedrock` is different: it has no static credential header. The secret's value is a JSON AWS credential (`{"accessKeyId":"…","secretAccessKey":"…","sessionToken":"…"}`) and KnoxCall computes the SigV4 signature server-side over the finalized request, so the AWS secret access key is never transmitted.

upstream_secret_id.description: The secret holding your provider credential. Required whenever `provider` is set.

upstream.description:
Base URL of the upstream, required for the providers whose endpoint is yours rather than the vendor's: `azure-openai`, `ollama`, `bedrock`, `openai-compatible`.

guardrail_webhook_url.description:
HTTPS endpoint your own scanner listens on (AIGW-45). Every prompt — and, in `response`/`both` mode, every response — is POSTed to it for a verdict before it moves.

What it receives is the REDACTED, post-tokenization body: the same bytes the provider would get, never a resolved provider credential and never your KnoxCall token. Shipping raw PHI to a third party to ask whether it contains PHI would be the leak the gateway exists to prevent.

The destination is resolved and refused at write time AND on every call — a private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata address is a 400, because DNS is not a promise.

Omit to send unsigned — the receiver then cannot prove the call came from KnoxCall.

AiGatewayRoutingPolicy.description:
How this agent retries and spreads load (AIGW-42). An empty object — the default for every agent — means one attempt per route and fail-over to `fallback_route_ids` on 5xx only, which is the behaviour the gateway has always had.

Every field is clamped server-side. A request parked waiting to retry occupies an API worker, so `max_attempts` caps at 5, any single delay at 30s, a honoured `Retry-After` at 60s, and the total sleep for one request at 60s regardless of how the fields combine.

jitter.description: Default true. Spreads each delay across 50–100% of its computed value so a fleet does not retry in lockstep.

route_weights.description: `{route_id: weight}`. The token's own capability scope is enforced on every candidate, so a weight can never reach a route the token was not granted.

AiGatewayPhantomToken.description: A capability (phantom) token row. The plaintext is never returned here — only at mint time.

prefix.description: The non-secret token prefix, safe to display.

scope_jsonb.description: The capability scope (providers/models) the token is bound to.

name.description: A human-readable label for the token.

dpop_required.description: Bind the token to a DPoP key. Requires `dpop_jkt`.

dpop_jkt.description: base64url SHA-256 thumbprint of your DPoP public key. Required when `dpop_required` is true.

expires_in_seconds.description: Token lifetime, clamped to [60s, 90d]. Omit for the 30 days default; a non-expiring token cannot be minted.

AiGatewayPhantomTokenCreated.description: The mint result. `token` is the plaintext capability token and is shown exactly once.

token.description: The plaintext capability token — store it now; it is never shown again.

unpriced_requests.description: Requests with no price data (excluded from cost).

AiGatewayFirewallRule.description: One heuristic rule inside a firewall policy.

name.description: 2-64 chars (letters, digits, space, underscore, hyphen). Appears in firewall events.

kind.description:
`regex` compiles the pattern with a linear-time engine (no lookahead, lookbehind or
backreferences). `keyword` is a case-insensitive substring match.

flags.description: Regex flags. Only i, m, s, g and y are accepted. Defaults to i. Ignored for keyword rules.

AiGatewayFirewallPolicy.description: A tenant-scoped prompt-firewall policy, attachable to agents and MCP servers.

version.description: Bumped when a policy is re-created under the same name.

heuristics.description: Tenant rules. The built-in prompt-injection patterns always run in addition to these.

canary_enabled.description: Inject a canary token into the system prompt and flag it if the model echoes it back.

name.description: 2-64 chars. Re-using an existing name creates the next version.

skipped.description: Rules that could not be compiled and so did not run. Always empty for a validated request.

AiGatewayUsage.description: Cost and token rollup by model over the requested period.

group.description: The dimension value for this row (e.g. a model id, provider name, or tag value).

AiGatewayUsageExport.description: FinOps showback/chargeback rollup, aggregated by the requested dimension.

OAuthTokenRequest.description: OAuth 2.1 token request (RFC 6749 §4, RFC 8628 §3.4). Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

client_id.description: The OAuth client identifier. Required for public clients; confidential clients may instead use HTTP Basic auth.

client_secret.description: The OAuth client secret (confidential clients only).

redirect_uri.description: Must match the redirect URI used in the authorization request (`authorization_code` grant).

code_verifier.description: PKCE code verifier (RFC 7636). Required for public clients using the `authorization_code` grant.

device_code.description: The device code (for the device-code grant).

scope.description: Space-delimited list of granted scopes (may be narrower than requested).

refresh_token.description: A refresh token, when the grant issues one.

tenant.description: The tenant the token is scoped to.

client_id.description: The client the token was issued to.

OAuthIntrospectRequest.description: OAuth token introspection request (RFC 7662 §2.1). Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

token_type_hint.description: Hint about the type of the token submitted.

active.description: Whether the token is currently active (not expired, not revoked, and known).

require_dpop.description:
Non-standard member (RFC 7662 §2.2 permits extensions). `true` when the
token's owning client is configured to require DPoP-bound tokens. A
resource server MUST refuse a token whose `cnf.jkt` is absent while this
is `true` — KnoxCall's own data plane and `/v1` API both do.

tenant.description: The tenant the token is scoped to.

OAuthRevokeRequest.description: OAuth token revocation request (RFC 7009 §2.1). Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

token_type_hint.description: Hint about the type of the token submitted.

OAuthDeviceAuthorizationRequest.description: OAuth device authorization request (RFC 8628 §3.1). Sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

user_code.description: The end-user verification code to enter at `verification_uri`.

verification_uri_complete.description: The verification URI with the `user_code` pre-filled (optional, RFC 8628).

expires_in.description: Lifetime of the `device_code` and `user_code` in seconds.

interval.description: Minimum seconds the client should wait between polling `POST /oauth/token`.

AiGatewayTokenExchangeRequest.description:
RFC 8693 token-exchange request for `POST /v1/oauth/token`. Sent as
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (RFC 6749) or `application/json`.

subject_token.description:
The workload's OIDC id_token, JWS-compact. Its `iss` must match a registered
binding, its signature must verify against that issuer's published JWKS, and it
must be unexpired. Where single-use enforcement is on, a second exchange of the
same token is `invalid_grant`.

audience.description: Defaults to `knoxcall:gateway`. Any other value is `invalid_target`.

resource.description:
RFC 8707 resource indicator — the `resource` value from an MCP server's
create/get response. Supplying it narrows the minted token to `tool` kind and
binds that resource into the capability HMAC, so the token reaches exactly that
one MCP server and nothing else. Omit it for an `agent`-kind token for the
`/v1/ai` plane. A repeated or non-string value is `invalid_target` — it is never
silently dropped, because dropping it would mint an UNCONFINED token while the
client believes it is audience-restricted.

AiGatewayTokenExchangeResponse.description:
RFC 8693 §2.2.1 response. This is a bare OAuth body, NOT the `{data, meta}` envelope
the rest of `/v1` returns — an OAuth client parses this shape.

access_token.description:
The capability token, returned ONCE. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
to `/v1/ai` (agent kind) or `/v1/mcp/<slug>` (tool kind, resource-bound).

expires_in.description: Lifetime in seconds, from the binding's `access_token_ttl_seconds` (default 900).

scope.description:
The capability scope, JSON-encoded, for visibility only. The source of truth is
the capability HMAC bound into the token — editing this string changes nothing.

AiGatewayDataPlaneError.description:
AIGW-163 — the ONE error envelope of the AI data plane, served by `/v1/ai/*` and by
every layer in front of it (authentication, the audience guard, the rate limiter,
the boot sentinel).

It is NOT the `{error: {type, message, request_id}}` envelope the rest of `/v1`
uses. That one belongs to the Management API, which is a different plane with a
different credential; this one is what a governed proxy can answer beside a
provider's own body. `/v1/mcp` answers JSON-RPC 2.0 and `/v1/oauth/token` answers
RFC 6749 §5.2, both by their protocols' rules.

**`error` and `code` always carry the same value.** That is deliberate: three
incompatible shapes existed here before AIGW-163 and they disagreed about which of
the two was machine-readable, so both are now, and a client that reads either keeps
working. Branch on the identifier, never on `error_description` — descriptions are
rewritten whenever a clearer wording is found.

Some refusals add extra keys alongside the three (`utilization_pct`, `model`,
`request_id`). Ignore keys you do not recognise; new ones are additive.

OAuthError.description: OAuth 2.1 error response (RFC 6749 §5.2). The OAuth endpoints use this shape rather than the /v1 `ErrorResponse` envelope.

error.description: A single ASCII error code from RFC 6749 §5.2 / RFC 8628 §3.5 / RFC 8693 §2.2.2.

error_uri.description: URI of a human-readable web page with error information.

X-Request-Id.description:
Unique identifier for this request (UUID). Present on **every** response and equal
to the `request_id` field in the response body. Quote it when contacting support.

KnoxCall-Version.description:
The dated API version (`YYYY-MM-DD`) that served this response. Equals the value
of the `KnoxCall-Version` request header when supplied, otherwise the newest version.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description:
Maximum requests allowed per window. Emitted on every response whenever a rate
limit is configured for the authenticated key.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description:
Remaining requests in the current window. Emitted on every response whenever a rate
limit is configured for the authenticated key.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description:
Epoch seconds at which the current rate-limit window resets. Emitted on every
response whenever a rate limit is configured for the authenticated key.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Set on `429` responses.

X-Idempotent-Replay.description:
Set to `true` when this response is a replayed copy of a previously completed
request that carried the same idempotency key.

AiGatewayDataPlaneError.description:
A refusal on the AI data plane, in the one envelope every layer answers with
(AIGW-163). The HTTP status carries the class; `code` carries the cause.

**400** a policy you configured refused the request — nothing changes on a retry.
**401** the credential was rejected; mint a new token. **403** the credential is
valid but not permitted to do this. **404** no agent with that slug for this
tenant. **422** understood and unprocessable (batch envelope the gateway cannot
screen, output-schema violation). **429** a ceiling was reached — retry after
`Retry-After`. **500** our fault. **502** the provider failed after every configured
failover hop. **503** a control could not be applied, so the request was refused
rather than served ungoverned — almost never "the gateway is down"; read the code.

The complete code list, and what to do about each, is on the
[errors page](https://docs.knoxcall.com/ai-gateway/errors).

X-Request-Id.description: Correlation id for this call — the key into the `ai_gateway.request_denied` audit row that explains it. Quote it in support requests.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until this refusal could succeed. Sent when the server KNOWS the answer — a spend cap counts to its UTC daily/monthly rollover, a rate limit to the end of its window — and omitted rather than guessed when it does not.

X-Auth-Failure.description: On an authentication or authorization refusal, the same value as `code`. Lets a client or a proxy classify the failure without reading the body.

budgetExceeded.summary: 429 — the agent's daily cap is spent (carries Retry-After)

expiredToken.summary: 401 — the credential was rejected (also in X-Auth-Failure)

firewallBlock.summary: 400 — a prompt-firewall rule matched under a `block` policy

value.error_description: Request blocked by firewall policy: system-prompt-extraction

piiPolicyDegraded.summary: 503 — a control could not be applied, so nothing was forwarded

value.error_description: One or more PII recognizers failed to compile, so redaction would be only partly applied. The request was refused rather than forwarded unprotected.

Unauthorized.description: Authentication is required or the provided API key is invalid.

error.message: API key is required. Use Authorization: Bearer <api_key> or x-api-key header.
Invalid API key.

RouteDestinationLocked.description:
The write would give a route that carries a standing `decrypt` or `detokenize` field
action a destination it does not already store (or switch on one it stores but does not
send to), and this credential may not open those
values. `forbidden` — a token issued to a person (refused whatever the role: make the
change from the dashboard as an Owner or Admin), or a key whose policy lacks the action's
own permission (`transit:decrypt` / `vaults:detokenize`). `insufficient_scope` — an OAuth
token narrowed to scopes that do not include the action's own scope; the
`WWW-Authenticate` header names it. Nothing was written. Not retryable as is.

person_token.summary: A token issued to a person

error.message: A token issued to a person (knoxcall login, a device or authorization-code grant) cannot change where this route sends: it carries a decrypt or detokenize action, so its destination receives the opened values. Change it from the dashboard as an Owner or Admin (it asks for a fresh second factor), or use a machine credential that holds the action's own permission (transit:decrypt or vaults:detokenize).

insufficient_scope.summary: A narrowed token without the action's scope

error.message: This access token was granted [routes:write] and does not include transit:decrypt. This route carries a standing `decrypt` action, so changing where it sends needs that scope.

Forbidden.description:
The key is authenticated but not authorized for this action (missing scope), a plan
limit was reached, or the resource must be managed via OAuth (`use_oauth`) / is a
protected system client (`system_client_protected`).

error.message: This key is not authorized to list AI gateways.
This resource must be managed with an OAuth 2.1 access token.
This client is managed by the platform and cannot be modified.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

error.message: Route not found.

ValidationError.description: The request failed validation (always `400 validation_error`). A malformed idempotency key returns `400 invalid_idempotency_key`.

error.message: name and target_base_url are required.
X-Idempotency-Key must be a non-empty string of at most 255 characters.

McpUnprocessable.description:
The MCP server definition was refused. `plaintext_auth` — an `auth.headers`
value is a literal credential rather than a `{{secret_id:<uuid>}}`
reference. `validation` — `upstream_url` is not a public https address, or
a field failed validation. `unsupported_server_type` — `collection` is not
served yet.

error.message: auth.headers["Authorization"] must reference a KnoxCall secret, e.g. "Bearer {{secret_id:<uuid>}}".

blocked_destination.summary: upstream_url resolves to a private address

error.message: upstream_url is not a valid MCP destination: "169.254.169.254" is in a private/reserved range.
server_type 'collection' is not served yet - an MCP server must proxy an upstream MCP server (server_type 'upstream').

Conflict.description: A resource with the same unique identifier already exists, or the resource is in use.

error.message: A route with this name already exists.

ClientNameConflictOrRequestInProgress.description:
Either of two conflicts, distinguished by `error.type`:

* `conflict` — a client with this name already exists in the caller's own
  data space. Client names are unique per `(tenant, name, Live/Test)`, so
  the same machine MAY be registered under one name in both Live and Test,
  but not twice within one of them. Choose a different name; retrying the
  same one will never succeed.
* `request_in_progress` — a request with the same idempotency key is still
  being processed. Retry after a short delay; do not change the body.

error.message: A client with this name already exists.

InterceptRouteConflict.description:
`intercept_route_conflict` — the request would turn `intercept_enabled` on for a route
whose upstream host and base path another intercept-enabled route already covers in the
same environment. Only one route may take a host's traffic under route-aware
interception: turn the flag off on the route the message names, or leave it off here.

error.message: Route "hubspot-crm" already intercepts api.hubapi.com/crm/v3 in production. Turn Intercept off on that route first, or leave it off on this one.

RequestInProgress.description:
A request with the same idempotency key is still being processed. Retry after a
short delay; do not change the request body.

error.message: A request with this idempotency key is already in progress.

IdempotencyKeyReuse.description:
The supplied idempotency key was already used for a request with a different body.
Idempotency keys may only be reused with an identical request.

error.message: This idempotency key was already used with a different request body.

PlanLimit.description:
Payment Required. The action exceeds your plan's limits. Two `error.type` values
share this status: `plan_limit` when a COUNTED resource quota was reached (routes,
secrets, AI agents, MCP servers), and `plan_feature` when the CAPABILITY itself is
not on your tier (custom PII redaction policies, compliance packs, custom
prompt-firewall policies). Both mean "upgrade to proceed"; branch on `type` only if
you want to distinguish "you have used your allowance" from "buy a bigger plan".

Neither ever revokes something you already have: a plan downgrade leaves existing
agents, policies and installed packs in place and keeps working.

error.message: Route limit reached (10). Upgrade your plan to add more.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests. Retry after the indicated time. The `X-RateLimit-*` headers are
also present on non-429 responses whenever a limit is configured.

error.message: API rate limit exceeded. Please retry later.

RateLimiterUnavailable.description:
The rate-limit counter store is unreachable, so the request was refused rather
than admitted unmetered. This is NOT an over-spend — the limit was never
measured — which is why it is a 503 and not a 429: an SDK should treat it as a
transient server fault and retry with backoff, honouring `Retry-After`.

error.message: The workflow execution rate-limit store is unavailable. Runs are refused rather than launched unmetered.
An unexpected error occurred.
